text:
oliver: Quick sync 15min: assemble a compact benchmark narrative for launch collateral. Deliver: 3 visuals, 2 headline A/Bs, sample lead routing + short sales calc. Keep claims conservative.
tess: agree. lean into two tests: latency-focused and cost-focused. also include a tiny ops curve for concurrency.
arjun: chart ideas (short):
- Chart 1: cost curve vs concurrency
  ```
  x: concurrent requests
  y: $ per 10k tokens
  curves: hosted, dedicated (reserved), dedicated (autoscale)
  note: show knee point where reserved becomes cheaper
  ```
- Chart 2: tail delta by slice
  ```
  x: percentile (p50,p75,p90,p95,p99)
  y: latency (ms)
  lines: short-chat, long-agent, embed-lookup
  callout: p95 SLA line at 150ms
  ```
- Chart 3: micro-slice unit cost bars
  ```
  rows: short-chat, long-agent, embeddings
  bars: baseline vs prefix-cache vs batching+quant
  metric: $ per request (normalized for typical tokens/req)
  ```
maria: copy directions: want two headline tones \u2014 "Engineer-first" and "Customer outcome". keep hero language non-exact: use "up to" ranges.
oliver: headline A (engineer-first): "Bench-backed serving: predictable p95s and clear unit economics for production."
tess: headline B (customer outcome): "Faster answers, smaller bills 1012 see where most savings come from."
arjun: social microcopy suggestions:
- short: "We ran a lab across real slices: median latency down to ~100ms, unit cost down to ~40% of baseline. Try your prompts."
- alternative: "How low can inference cost go without hurting p95? Our lab shows practical tradeoffs."
maria: sales calc snippet (one-liner): "Hosted baseline: $0.00045/token => $450 per 1M tokens. Typical cache+batch -> ~45% lower => ~$248 per 1M. Show per-10k on cheat-sheet."
oliver: routing rules (simple):
- auto-tag bench on prompt upload or "run benchmark" request
- demo-route if expected monthly tokens > 10M or asks private deploy
- enterprise if legal/compliance flags present (SAML, VPC)
- bench-inbox receives CSV + PNGs from bench-bot for review
tess: A/B testing plan for headlines: roll both to small landing test (2k visitors) measure CTR and demo requests. Use conservative phrasing in hero; put exact numbers in appendix.
arjun: bench-bot run example we can share with customers:
```bash
/bench run --model redwood-rtd-v2 --slices short,long,embed --tokens 4000 --concurrency 8 --seeds 3 --cache on --quant off --out ./bench_out
```
bench-bot: queued a micro-run when `/bench` called. quick-run returns CSV, PNGs, and a 2-line summary. flags: --cache, --quant, --concurrency. use `/bench share` to email results.
maria: creative notes: ask designers to leave space for one-sentence appendix and a tiny table mapping "app type -> recommended config" (chat: keep warm KV; agent: RX batching; embeddings: async pooling).
oliver: webinar hook draft: "Lab-backed playbook: measuring p95 and cost for real LLM workloads 1; bring a prompt set and we'll slice it live." CTA: "Upload prompts when you RSVP."
tess: two email subject lines: "See latency + cost for your prompts" and "How much can you save on inference? (bench results inside)"
arjun: quick internal example for a PR/social card: "Benchroom: median 100ms, up to 55% unit cost reduction on common slices. Live lab at launch." (note: conservative "up to")
maria: timeline: mock visuals by Mon EOD, A/B headlines & copy Tue, quick webinar dry-run Wed. bench-bot will post PNGs here when runs finish.
bench-bot: micro-runs queued (2 jobs). ETA ~35m. outputs: 3 PNGs + per-request CSV + short_summary.txt. use `/bench status` to see progress.
oliver: ok team. deliverables checklist for the thread: visuals (light/dark variants), one short social card, 2 headline A/Bs, sales cheat-sheet (per-1k & per-1M), webinar blurb, routing bullets, bench commands for customers. keep deliverable copy <=2 lines each.
tess: pairing: arjun + infra to run the lab; maria to draft landing + email copy; oliver to own routing playbook and webinar.
arjun: starting first micro-run now. will post results and a CSV link. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: will draft appendix table and paste here after visuals.
oliver: perfect. close the loop once bench-bot posts PNGs. thanks!
